description:
Programme or Project Overview

UMCG is hiring a mechatronics engineer for the cryogenic kidney preservation programme, a research-driven technical role developing equipment that keeps donor kidneys viable at extremely low temperatures. The role sits at the interface of medical device engineering and transplant research, contributing to systems that are being developed to extend organ preservation windows beyond what current static cold storage allows.

The engineer will design, build and test electromechanical subsystems for cryogenic preservation devices, work with cryogenic fluids and temperature-controlled components, and collaborate with surgeons, cryobiologists and clinical technologists on experimental setups. The appointment is a salaried staff position under the CAO-UMC collective agreement with a gross monthly salary between EUR 3,897 and EUR 5,341 depending on experience.

What the work involves

Day-to-day work spans mechatronic design and prototyping, sensor and control integration, testing under cryogenic conditions and documentation aligned with medical-technology quality expectations. The position offers a unique combination of hands-on engineering and translational research, with results feeding directly into clinical studies on organ preservation. Candidates bring a degree in mechatronics, mechanical or electrical engineering and demonstrable experience with precision instrument development; affinity with clinical environments and multidisciplinary teams is essential.

Highlights

  • Mechatronic design of cryogenic preservation hardware
  • Sensor, control and instrumentation integration
  • Testing and prototyping under low-temperature conditions
  • Collaboration with clinical and cryobiology researchers
  • Documentation in a medical-technology context
  • Salaried staff position, EUR 3,897 - 5,341 gross per month

About University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG)

UMCG is one of the largest university medical centres in the Netherlands and the academic hospital of the University of Groningen. It combines patient care with biomedical research and graduate education, organised around research institutes covering neuroscience, oncology, ageing, regenerative medicine and population health. The centre employs PhD candidates and postdocs on salaried contracts under the Dutch collective agreement for university medical centres (CAO-UMC). Research and clinical vacancies, including physician-researcher tracks and technical R&D roles, are published on its recruitment portal werkenbijumcg.nl.
